articles.title: Got a letter from the Clean Power Alliance and have solar on your roof? Here are some considerations.
articles.image_alt: Rooftop solar panels on a La Cañada Flintridge house with the San Gabriel Mountains behind
articles.image_prompt: Editorial documentary photograph for a local news article about rooftop solar in La Cañada Flintridge. Quiet suburban foothill house with dark roof and neat grid of black solar panels, late afternoon light, San Gabriel mountains soft in the background. No logos, no text, no people.
articles.excerpt: If you live in La Cañada Flintridge and got a letter from Clean Power Alliance (CPA), you are not losing your solar. The city picked CPA as the company that makes the power. Southern California Edison (SCE) still delivers it over the wires. You will keep getting one bill from SCE.

articles.title: Front-row seats to orbit: How La Cañada Flintridge watches SpaceX from the driveway
articles.image_alt: Twilight Falcon 9 exhaust plume forming a space jellyfish over the foothills
articles.image_prompt: Photorealistic twilight photo of a Falcon 9 space jellyfish over the San Gabriel foothills. Deep blue sky, thin orange horizon only. High up: a slender twisting white corkscrew vapor trail that opens into a soft milky-white ice-blue translucent exhaust bloom.
articles.excerpt: As a resident of La Cañada Flintridge, you already have something most of the country has to book a flight for: front-row access to rocket launches tied to the engineers in your own community.

articles.title: The little-known origin of JPL: Caltech’s Suicide Squad got kicked into a wash and founded the space age
articles.image_alt: Early rocket motor experiment in the Arroyo Seco, 1936
articles.excerpt: Here is the part the Mars rover press releases never lead with. NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory did not begin as a gleaming federal campus on Oak Grove Drive.
